To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Piezo-ICPI using flat-tipped pipettes with a wall of 0.62 μm improves the clinical efficiency of IPI.
the Piezo ICSI using flat-tipped pipettes with a wall of 0.6 μm significantly improved the oocyte survival rate, fertilization rate, and good-quality day-2 embryo rate.
the Piezo ICSI using micropipette with a wall thickness (WT) of 0.6 μm significantly improved the clinical efficiency of ICSI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical efficiency of the Piezo- ICSI method and the improvement of the Piezo ICSI method for human oocyte.
the development of an improved Piezo- ICSI method for human oocyte.
the improvement of clinical efficiency in Piezo-ICSE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IPI is a more efficient method than the CI and CPI.
the Piezo method with the flat-tipped microneedle is superior to the conventional method in terms of clinical outcomes.
the use of micropipettes having a wall thickness of ≤0.625 µm is a significant improvement over the conventional micropipettes used in the conventional ICSI and Piezo-ICSi.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of flat-tipped microneedles with a wall thickness less than 1 μM is essential for Piezo-ICSE.
Piezo-ICPI with micropipettes of 0.6 μm wall thickness is the best method for human ICSI.
Piezo-ICPI is a useful and effective technique for ICSI, which can be applied to the treatment of male infertility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of micropipettes that are 1 μM in diameter with a wall thickness 0.625 micrometer is the most efficient for Piezo-ICSi.
IPI is a useful method for improving the efficiency of ICSI.
the Piezo method is more efficient than the conventional ICSI method.
